conviction_note: Close to a non-result. The quarter's volume headwinds (Toyota's July and August output down, China ICE demand collapsing, the Kumamoto quake stoppage in early August) are public, and the stock has already fallen about 9% since 2026-09-28. Against that, H1 USD/JPY averaged about 159 versus a 150 plan, and the plan carries a 15bn yen Middle East buffer, so the full-year forecast is more likely held than cut. A Toyota-group peer held its guidance on a weak H1 and fell 2.9%, which tilts the reaction slightly negative. The findings sum to -0.2 and the scaled number is -0.18 (p_up 48 x abs 4.5); the two agree.
bar: IFIS consensus via kabuyoho (2026-10-28): FY3/2027 OP 239.3bn yen and pretax 255.5bn, against a company plan of 235bn / 245bn; H1 pretax consensus 100.6bn, which implies Q2 pretax of about 52.8bn after Q1's 47.8bn. https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=7259 and https://kabuyoho.jp/report?bcode=7259 . The company gives no H1 plan, only a full year (Q1 tanshin, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260731/140120260730504134.pdf). The H1 pretax consensus is one source (IFIS) with no second estimate to check it against, so the quarter-level findings are kept small.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0% (no holder at or above 0.5%), unchanged, as of 2026-10-28 (https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html, per the baseline). 信用倍率 6.96 (kabutan, 2026-10-29), so leveraged retail is crowded long, which is the one setup in which a visible miss still finds sellers. No options, so no skew. Run-up -7.79% over 20 days and -4.95% over 5. priced_lean_pct -0.03: the margin overhang (-0.42) offsets the run-up term (+0.39).

findings.finding: Q2 volume headwinds are visible in public series. Toyota's global production fell 5.9% in August (overseas -7.6%) and its China sales fell 22.8%, the second straight monthly decline. In Q1 Aisin's PT units were already 210k below plan, mainly China. The 2026-07-28 Kumamoto quake stopped Aisin Kyushu and halted Toyota's Kyushu plants and its Tahara line on 3-7 August. Together this points to Q2 coming in below the roughly 52.8bn yen Q2 pretax implied by IFIS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At Q1 (2026-07-31, 13:00) pretax missed IFIS by 20.1% and the stock fell 11.71% (traders.co.jp / kabuyoho). At the 2025-10-31 H1, a beat with the plan held, the estimated reaction was +3.91% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the Toyota monthly figures are public and the stock has fallen from 2,241.5 (09-28) to about 2,036 with no company news. If this were fully priced, IFIS H1 pretax would sit below the prior year's 106.4bn by more than it does (it is 100.6bn) and the 2,585 consensus target would have been cut further. What remains is the size of the Q2 miss against a consensus that still implies Q2 up on Q1.
findings.independence: Aisin's own Q1 Q&A (PT units 210k below plan, China AT demand the main concern, Kumamoto costs to be disclosed later): https://www.aisin.com/jp/investors/settlement/fy2027_q1_minutes-j_2.pdf ; Kumamoto stoppage reports: https://kumanichi.com/articles/2019401 ; MONOist on Japanese automakers' China output halving in July: https://monoist.itmedia.co.jp/mn/spv/2609/17/news018.html

findings.finding: The FX and buffer cushion makes a held full-year forecast the likely outcome. The plan assumes 150 yen to the dollar, while H1 actually averaged about 159 (the H1 rate Toyota-group peer Tokai Rika reported on 10-28). Aisin's plan bridge implies about 1.7bn yen of OP per yen of USD per year, so roughly +7-8bn vs plan in H1 on the dollar alone. The 235bn OP plan also embeds a separate -15bn yen Middle East risk line. Management said in July that it had no need to change the volume plan, and that the quake would not trigger a downward revision.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior H1 forecast decisions: 2023-10-31 raised; 2024-10-31 cut (OP 220 to 200bn, estimated reaction -5.12%); 2025-10-31 held on a strong H1 (+3.91% estimated). Revision dates from kabuyoho's 修正履歴; the reactions are the baseline's estimated-cadence history.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock has de-rated into the print as if a cut were possible: down 9% in a month, with four brokers cutting target prices since August. A hold of 235bn against the street's 239bn would be a mild relief rather than a miss, and that only applies if the market fears a cut, which the drawdown suggests.
findings.independence: Tokai Rika's H1 summary (H1 USD at 159, H2 assumption at 150, FY plan held): https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261028/140120261027557215.pdf ; Aisin's Q1 Q&A (no change to annual volume plan, quake not a reason to cut): https://www.aisin.com/jp/investors/settlement/fy2027_q1_minutes-j_2.pdf

findings.finding: The Toyota-group peer that reported first sets the reaction function. Tokai Rika (6995) reported H1 OP -17.7% and pretax -29.9% at 14:40 on 10-28, held its full-year plan with an H2 USD assumption of 150, and was trading -2.92% at 10:14 on 10-29. Stanley Electric, which reported on 10-26, was -0.99%. A weak H1 held at a conservative FX rate is being sold, not bought, in this group this week.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for Aisin on peer read-through. Aisin's own last print fell 11.71% on a miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The read-through is only one session old, and Aisin itself is already -1.6% this morning before its release, so part of it is in the sealed spot. What is left is whether Aisin's release looks like Tokai Rika's (weak H1, hold). That is the most likely shape, and the peer says that shape trades down.
findings.independence: Same shape across the group: Tokai Rika's tanshin, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261028/140120261027557204.pdf ; Stanley quote, https://kabutan.jp/stock/?code=6923 . Both rest on peers' prices, not on an Aisin document.

findings.finding: The buyback is ongoing and still has room. 64.0bn of the 100bn yen authority had been used by 2026-09-30 (7.83bn in September in the open market), so about 36bn remains to March, a steady bid of roughly 2.4% of market cap. A new programme at H1 is unlikely: neither of the last two H1 prints carried a returns announcement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-04-28 FY print carried the 100bn buyback plus a tender offer, and the estimated reaction was +7.96%. The 2025-10-31 H1 carried no returns news.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since the programme is public. The only upside is a top-up or an acceleration announced with the H1 results, which the release pattern argues against.
findings.independence: Q1 presentation: shareholder-return policy, 75 yen dividend, 100bn buyback ( https://www.aisin.com/jp/investors/settlement/fy2027_q1_presentation-f-j.pdf ). Same company, a different document.

outside_window.finding: Possible later forecast pressure if China AT demand and the BMW e-axle ramp keep slipping. Management said in July it could not rule out volume risk on the BMW programme, which launches in the second half of FY2026. Any cut beyond this print resolves at Q3 (around early February 2027).

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: a hold is most likely (FX cushion plus the Middle East buffer, and management's July stance), a cut is possible on China volumes, and the street at OP 239bn / pretax 255bn sits slightly above the 235/245 plan. Returns: no new action expected, with 36bn of the buyback still running and the 35 yen interim dividend already planned. New-year guide: not applicable at H1. Quarter vs own 進捗率: H1 OP took 42% of the full year in FY26 and 28% in FY25 (both H2-weighted); Q1 is at 15.6% of plan against 20.9% a year earlier.
baseline_tension: The findings mostly agree with the tape: down 7.8% over 20 days, a crowded margin long, a weak peer reaction. The strongest positive the release could carry is a held full-year forecast with a raised FX assumption, set against a stock that has de-rated 9% in a month (a 悪材料出尽くし setup). I looked for it and filed it at +0.5, so the net is close to zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has): the Toyota-production and China-volume finding was cut from -0.6 to -0.4, and p_up moved from 46 to 48.
Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): I had already looked for and filed the strongest positive (a held forecast on the FX cushion, +0.5) and the buyback (+0.1), so this rule moved nothing further.
